description.text:
This protocol lets a layer-shell client hand interactive move and
resize over to the compositor: the client starts an operation with
begin_resize or begin_move, the compositor drives the surface size or
position through layer-surface configure events, and reports state,
rejection reasons, and placement through this interface.

The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not",
"should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this
document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.
description.summary: layer surface interactive move and resize integration for treeland

description.text:
This interface allows a layer-shell client (typically a dock
surface) to opt in to compositor-driven interactive move and
resize, so the compositor owns the drag state machine and the
client follows the resulting layer-surface configure events
instead of racing its own set_size requests.

This protocol applies to any layer-shell surface. The compositor
drives the surface's size (begin_resize) or position (begin_move)
over an interactive drag; whether a particular axis is freely
resizable depends on the concrete anchor configuration.
description.summary: manager for layer surface interactive move and resize

description.text:
Destroy the manager object. This does not destroy layer shell
objects created with get_layer_shell_extension_object; those remain
valid until their wl_surface is destroyed or the client
destroys them.
description.summary: destroy the layer shell extension manager

description.text:
Create a layer shell extension object for an existing wl_surface. The
surface is expected to be a layer-shell surface; the compositor
reports layer_shell_extension_exists if the same wl_surface already has
a layer shell extension object bound.

The layer shell extension object is tied to the wl_surface: when the
wl_surface is destroyed, the
treeland_layer_shell_extension_object_v1 object is destroyed by
the compositor as well, and the client must call
get_layer_shell_extension_object again for a new wl_surface. A
layer shell extension object must not outlive its wl_surface.
description.summary: create a layer shell extension object for an existing wl_surface

entries.name: layer_shell_extension_exists
entries.summary: the wl_surface already has a layer shell extension object bound

entries.name: wl_surface_invalid
entries.summary: the get_layer_shell_extension_object wl_surface argument is invalid

description.text:
The client starts an interactive resize with begin_resize, passing
a serial from a recent pointer event. The compositor validates the
serial, takes over the drag (like xdg_toplevel.resize) and drives
the surface size through the standard layer-surface configure
events, reporting the resize state and any size restrictions
through this interface.

The client may also start an interactive move with begin_move; the
exact move semantics and state reporting are not yet finalized.
description.summary: compositor-driven interactive resize and move for a layer surface
destroy the layer shell extension object

description.text:
Start a compositor-driven interactive resize of the associated
surface. The seat and serial must come from a recent pointer
button press on that seat; an invalid serial makes the
compositor reject the request with resize_error.bad_serial.
edges names which edge (or corner) of the surface the client
wants to drag, using the xdg_toplevel.resize_edge values. The
client owns which edge it drags; the compositor executes the
drag on the reported edge.

The compositor rejects the request with resize_error.bad_edges
when any of the requested edges is anchored: an anchored edge
is already fixed in place by the layer-shell layout, so
dragging it has no effect. A corner value (top_left etc.)
requires both of its edges to be unanchored, otherwise the
request is rejected. A dock anchored to a single screen edge,
for example, may only be dragged on the edge opposite to its
anchor.

Any other value is rejected with resize_error.bad_edges. The
compositor emits resizing(1) once the drag actually starts,
resizing(0) when it ends, and drives the surface size through
the standard layer-surface configure events. On a rejected
request it emits resize_rejected with a resize_error reason;
in that case no resize starts and resizing is never emitted
for this request. A request on a destroyed surface or with a
destroyed seat is also rejected, with resize_error.bad_surface
or resize_error.bad_seat respectively.

The min/max size arguments bound this resize only: they apply
while this drag is active and are not a persistent property
of the surface. A value of 0 means no limit in that direction
(minimum 0 / maximum unbounded); negative values are treated
as 0. The compositor clamps the target size to these limits
and reflects the clamped size through the standard
layer-surface configure event. Invalid limits (min > max with
both non-zero) are ignored for that axis.

args.name: seat
args.summary: seat the resize is initiated from

args.name: serial
args.summary: serial of a recent pointer button press on seat

args.name: edges
args.summary: edge(s) the client wants to drag, none of which may be anchored

args.name: min_width
args.summary: minimum width for this resize, 0 for none

args.name: min_height
args.summary: minimum height for this resize, 0 for none

args.name: max_width
args.summary: maximum width for this resize, 0 for none

args.name: max_height
args.summary: maximum height for this resize, 0 for none

description.text:
resizing=1 when the compositor starts the interactive drag,
resizing=0 when it ends. The client may use this to run a
settle / spring animation after the drag finishes. resizing(1)
is only emitted after the compositor has actually taken over
the drag; rejected begin_resize requests instead cause a
resize_rejected event.

args.name: resizing
args.summary: 1 during interactive resize, 0 after it ends

description.text:
Emitted when a begin_resize request is rejected: the reason
names a resize_error value. No resize starts and resizing is
never emitted for the rejected request. The client should use
this instead of inferring acceptance from the absence of a
resizing(1) event, and may fall back to its own drag logic.

Values indicate which edge (or corner) of the surface is being
dragged in a resize operation, named from the surface's own
perspective. Values are bit flags matching
xdg_toplevel.resize_edge exactly: 1=top, 2=bottom, 4=left,
8=right; corner values are the OR of two adjacent edges
(top_left=5=1|4, bottom_left=6=2|4, top_right=9=1|8,
bottom_right=10=2|8).

The layer surface is anchored to one screen edge and changes
height, vertical surfaces (left/right) change width. Whether an
edge may be dragged at all depends on the surface's anchor; see
begin_resize.

begin_resize is rejected (no resize starts) when the serial is
stale (bad_serial), the edges value is not a valid resize_edge
(bad_edges), or the compositor cannot take over the resize
right now (inactive). It is also rejected when the associated
surface is invalid or has been destroyed (bad_surface), or
the seat is invalid or has been destroyed (bad_seat). The
compositor then emits resize_rejected with the reason; an
accepted request instead emits resizing(1).
description.summary: reason a begin_resize request was rejected

entries.name: bad_serial
entries.summary: serial does not match a recent pointer button press on the seat

entries.name: bad_edges
entries.summary: edges is not a valid resize_edge value

entries.name: inactive
entries.summary: the compositor cannot take over the resize right now (no container, surface not layer, animation running, or seat refused the takeover)

entries.name: bad_surface
entries.summary: the surface is invalid or has been destroyed

entries.name: bad_seat
entries.summary: the seat is invalid or has been destroyed
